title: Coherence of a tensor comparison normalized by its cochain square
statement:
theorem normalized_cochain_tensor_diagrams {X Y : Site.{u, w}}
    (f : RingedPullback.{u, u, u, u, u} Y.A X.A) (k : CochainPullback.Comparison.{u, u, u, u, u} f)
    (F : Y.D ⥤ X.D)
    (εc : DerivedCategory.Q ⋙ F ⟶ CochainPullback.pull f ⋙ DerivedCategory.Q)
    (nu : Y.closed.tensor ⋙ F ≅ (F.prod F) ⋙ X.closed.tensor)
    (huniversal : F.IsLeftDerivedFunctor εc
      (HomologicalComplex.quasiIso Y.modules (.up ℤ)))
    (hcomputes : ∀ P, Y.corner.mateFlat P → IsIso (εc.app P))
    (hnormalized : ∀ (P Q : CochainComplex Y.modules ℤ)
      (hP : Y.corner.mateFlat P) (hQ : Y.corner.mateFlat Q),
      ∃ (hP' : X.corner.mateFlat ((CochainPullback.pull f).obj P))
        (hQ' : X.corner.mateFlat ((CochainPullback.pull f).obj Q)),
        F.map (Y.model.iso Y.J Y.A Y.closed P Q hP.1 hQ.1).hom ≫
            nu.hom.app (DerivedCategory.Q.obj P, DerivedCategory.Q.obj Q) ≫
            X.closed.tensor.map (Prod.mkHom (εc.app P) (εc.app Q)) =
          εc.app (P ⊗ Q) ≫ DerivedCategory.Q.map (CochainPullback.comparison f k P Q).hom ≫
            (X.model.iso X.J X.A X.closed ((CochainPullback.pull f).obj P)
              ((CochainPullback.pull f).obj Q) hP'.1 hQ'.1).hom) :
    IsIso (cochainUnitComparison f k F εc) ∧
    (∀ M N P : Y.D,
      (nu).hom.app (Y.closed.tensor.obj (M, N), P) ≫
          X.closed.tensor.map (Prod.mkHom ((nu).hom.app (M, N))
            (𝟙 (F.obj P))) ≫
          (X.closed.monoidal.associator (F.obj M) (F.obj N) (F.obj P)).hom =
        F.map (Y.closed.monoidal.associator M N P).hom ≫
          (nu).hom.app (M, Y.closed.tensor.obj (N, P)) ≫
          X.closed.tensor.map (Prod.mkHom (𝟙 (F.obj M))
            ((nu).hom.app (N, P)))) ∧
    (∀ M : Y.D,
      (nu).hom.app (Y.closed.monoidal.tensorUnit, M) ≫
          X.closed.tensor.map (Prod.mkHom (cochainUnitComparison f k F εc) (𝟙 (F.obj M))) ≫
          (X.closed.monoidal.leftUnitor (F.obj M)).hom =
        F.map (Y.closed.monoidal.leftUnitor M).hom) ∧
    (∀ M : Y.D,
      (nu).hom.app (M, Y.closed.monoidal.tensorUnit) ≫
          X.closed.tensor.map (Prod.mkHom (𝟙 (F.obj M)) (cochainUnitComparison f k F εc)) ≫
          (X.closed.monoidal.rightUnitor (F.obj M)).hom =
        F.map (Y.closed.monoidal.rightUnitor M).hom) ∧
    (∀ M N : Y.D,
      (nu).hom.app (M, N) ≫
          (X.symmetry.toBraidedCategory.braiding (F.obj M) (F.obj N)).hom =
        F.map (Y.symmetry.toBraidedCategory.braiding M N).hom ≫
          (nu).hom.app (N, M))

proof.text: Descend the universal cochain counit through the homotopy quotient retaining its components. On the native flat-term K-flat class it is invertible by hypothesis. Resolve every homotopy object by a flat-term K-flat complex. Naturality of the counit and inversion of localized quasi-isomorphisms show that the localized ordinary pullback inverts quasi-isomorphisms within this class.

Right derivability of the module pushforward follows from Grothendieck abelianity and K-injective resolutions. Use the already proved helper CategoryTheory.exists_derived in RingedToposDerivedPushforwardComposition to construct the universal right-derived functor. The resolving-class adjunction theorem supplies a right adjoint to the specified F, with its actual descended universal counit. Construct a RingedTensorEdge using this adjunction and the ordinary comparison obtained field by field from k.

The hypothesis gives exactly the representative square for nu. Restrict the recorded tensor models using the bridge, and replace the homotopy comparison components by the original cochain components. The unique canonical tensor comparison on these representatives is therefore nu. The ordinary unit presentation identifies canonicalDerivedUnitComparison with cochainUnitComparison.

Apply canonicalTensorDiagrams to the constructed edge. Rewrite its tensor and unit maps by the previous identifications. Its associativity and symmetry are the required equations. Precompose each inverse-unitor identity by the image of the source forward unitor and postcompose by the target forward unitor; cancel the two inverse pairs to obtain the two forward-unitor equations.
